name: Black supremacy
summary: Black supremacy is a label for doctrines holding that black people are inherently superior to other races, best documented in the Nation of Islam under Elijah Muhammad (to 1975), which taught that whites were a bred race of devils whose 6,000-year rule had ended. Its program was rejection of integration, a separate black state funded by the former slave-owning nation, black economic self-reliance, strict moral and gender discipline, and refusal of military service.
scope: Represents the Nation of Islam under Elijah Muhammad (c. 1934-1975) as the best-documented black supremacist doctrine, with Malcolm X's 1963 statement of its program. Excludes the post-1975 mainstream Islam of W. Deen Mohammed, Black Hebrew Israelite groups, Nuwaubians, Rastafari and black nationalism that does not claim racial superiority, which differ in detail. Most answers outside race, separatism, religion and family are inferred and low confidence.

sources.usedFor: The Nation's own statement on separation, a separate state, self-defense, voting, intermarriage and economics.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Nation of Islam teaching stresses self-help and black-run institutions, and says nothing on state health systems; adherents are split between wanting state redress and distrusting the white-run government.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The movement's economic emphasis was on black-owned businesses and jobs it created itself, not on wage law; no stated position, so adherents plausibly split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Elijah Muhammad promoted black capitalism through bakeries, groceries and farms, yet also demanded state-funded reparations; no doctrine on markets versus government in general.

public-ownership.rationale: The program centred on black-owned private and collective enterprise and on distrust of the white-controlled federal government, so white-state ownership of industry fits poorly.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No documented position; the movement addressed racial rather than class redistribution, and Muhammad himself built an enterprise empire.

unions-good.rationale: The movement's focus was on racial self-reliance and black-owned jobs, with no documented stance on mostly white-led labor unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Nation bought land, farms and businesses and urged black people to own and control economic resources, implying respect for property, though it also demanded land from the state.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the movement criticized white economic domination but proposed black enterprise rather than regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: The Nation preached self-reliance and criticized dependence on white society, but also demanded state support and reparations for black Americans, so the answer is split.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective black-owned enterprise was encouraged, but no worker-ownership doctrine appears in the sources.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The Nation was itself under heavy state surveillance and saw white-run government as hostile; inferred from that distrust of authorities.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Elijah Muhammad enforced strict bans on alcohol, drugs and pork among members, treating intoxicants as a tool of black degradation.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The movement itself preached that whites are devils and saw white-state restrictions as hostile; inferred, with little direct statement.

strong-leader.rationale: Authority in the Nation rested on a single divine messenger, but the idea of a leader bypassing gridlock in a national government is not addressed.

state-harmful.rationale: The Nation demanded its own state and a separate territory, so it rejects statelessness even while condemning the existing white-run state.

limit-guns.rationale: Malcolm X for the Nation insisted black people have the right to defend themselves, and the Fruit of Islam served as a self-defense arm.

empower-police-military.rationale: Police are portrayed as successors to slave-era enforcers who traded bloodhounds for police dogs, and Muhammad told followers not to serve in the armed forces.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The Nation required sexual abstinence before marriage and monogamy within it, so legal sex work conflicts with its moral code.

decide-locally.rationale: Not addressed; the program wanted a separate nation rather than a position on decentralization within the existing state.

rehabilitation.rationale: The Nation recruited from prisons and promised moral reform through discipline and its teachings; inferred from that conversion-focused work.

traditional-family.rationale: Muhammad's teaching prescribed patriarchal roles, male providers, female homemakers, monogamy and chastity before marriage.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Heterosexual monogamy was required and gender roles strictly conservative; inferred as the Nation did not legislate on the point but its doctrine rules it out.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the pronatalist, conservative family doctrine and Muhammad's framing of black survival; no clear direct statement in the sources read.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Nation sought an Islam-based black nation and condemned Christianity as the white man's tool, so religion-informed public life is favored for its own faith, but a larger role for existing religion is not the aim.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Core demand: a separate state funded for 20 to 25 years by the former slave-owning nation, as redress for slavery.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The Nation taught conservative, essentialist gender roles; inferred from these teachings.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Nation rejected white American culture and sought its own black national culture, so the statement splits depending on which nation is meant. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

gradual-change.rationale: Malcolm X dismissed integration gains as tokenism and said white rule was scheduled to end, and Muhammad foresaw its imminent destruction.

reduce-immigration.rationale: No documented stance on immigration; the Nation's racial focus was on black Americans.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred: the movement distrusted white-led Western institutions, though it also sought outside Muslim support; no direct statement.

free-trade.rationale: No stated position; the Nation stressed black-owned enterprise and economic self-sufficiency.

nation-first.rationale: The Nation put the interests of the black nation first and rejected integration; inferred, since the 'country' in question is ambiguous.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The Nation opposed black men serving in white America's wars; inferred opposition to American-led interventions.

open-borders.rationale: The Nation's program is separation of the races into distinct territories, the opposite of open borders.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Environmental questions never addressed; the Nation's eschatology is of destruction through divine action, not policy.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Mixed: Yakub's story centres on a scientist, yet the Nation's expectation is divine intervention by the Mother Plane.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power never figures in the Nation's teaching; no basis for a position, so neutral.

revolution-justified.rationale: Elijah Muhammad taught that white rule would be ended by divine action and urged restraint, while Malcolm X asserted self-defense; adherents are split on human revolution.

central-planning.rationale: Muhammad built private and communal enterprises rather than planning; inferred, little direct evidence.

socialized-markets.rationale: The sources record no view on worker or public ownership of firms in a market economy; the Nation's own enterprises were run under the movement.

land-value-tax.rationale: Tax design never appears in Nation teaching or Malcolm X's statements, so there is nothing to infer from.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Nothing in the sources on inheritance; the movement's wealth question was racial redress, not taxation.

basic-income.rationale: Never addressed; the demand was for a funded separate state, with emphasis on self-reliance.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trade policy is never discussed in the sources; the economic emphasis was on black-owned local businesses.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's economic aims concerned black-owned institutions.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The Nation encouraged black ownership of land, shops and farms; inferred broad support for black owners.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The Nation ran businesses, paid work and tithes; abolition of money is foreign to its program.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary institutions are absent from the doctrine; no basis for either side.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognized bodies setting wages are not part of the Nation's program, which stressed self-help.

one-party-rule.rationale: Not addressed; the Nation was itself a religious body rather than a party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Inferred; the Nation's authority was a messenger of Allah, but hereditary rule of a state is not part of its program.

democracy-best.rationale: Muslims could register to vote and back chosen candidates, but integrationist democracy was viewed as tokenism and the Nation sought separation.

workers-councils.rationale: Inferred: no workers' council doctrine, and the movement was religious and racial rather than class-based.

right-to-secede.rationale: The central political demand was a separate territory for black Americans, a form of secession or partition.

natural-rulers.rationale: The doctrine calls black people the original divine race and says whites were allowed 6,000 years of rule; it ranks races by nature, but it does not say who is suited to govern.

political-violence-never.rationale: Malcolm X on behalf of the Nation asserted a right of self-defense, and the Fruit of Islam was a defense arm; Muhammad nonetheless held back from revolt.

war-builds-character.rationale: Muhammad told followers to refuse draft and military service in American wars.

separate-church-state.rationale: The goal was a separate nation under Islam, as Malcolm X described it, so state and religion are joined.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The Nation sought a nation ordered by its own Islamic teachings, though its scripture was distinctive.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred; the Nation wanted a state of its own with its own defense force.

military-superiority.rationale: Not addressed; Muhammad opposed black service in the US military, but a separate state's military was not detailed.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The separate-state demand and rejection of integration aim at a nation made up of black people, with whites kept separate.

class-struggle-history.rationale: History is explained as racial: whites were created to rule for 6,000 years, not by class struggle.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not addressed beyond the redress demand.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Never addressed; the Nation sought land for black Americans in the former slave states, not indigenous sovereignty.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Adherents demanded reparations from the nation that held slaves; inferred sympathy for colonial reparations, though the Nation focused on America.

civilizational-union.rationale: Pan-Africanism was rejected by Muhammad, though the Original Asiatic Nation concept spans non-European peoples; split.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Not addressed; the Nation stressed collective racial uplift and discipline.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The Nation imposed strict discipline and duty to the community on members; inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The doctrine concerns race, God and history, and says nothing about nature's value apart from humans.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred from the pronatalist, family-oriented stance and the notion of building a black nation.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The Nation blames white rule, not industrialization, for black suffering, and itself built farms and businesses; no clear stance.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The sources show no stance on technological disruption; the Mother Plane expectation is prophecy, not policy.

human-enhancement.rationale: The Nation favored strict bodily discipline and diet; inferred. Yakub's eugenic breeding is cast as the origin of evil.

algorithmic-government.rationale: AI governance is anachronistic for a movement of 1930 to 1975 and cannot be inferred from its principles.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption is anachronistic for the movement; its general distrust of state surveillance gives no firm answer.

restore-past-order.rationale: The Nation looked to a restored original black order, with white rule's 6,000 years ended; inferred from this return-to-origin framing.

direct-action.rationale: Muhammad urged separation and self-help instead of civil-rights marches and criticized King, but also confronted police at times; split.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources show no teaching that methods must mirror the desired society.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The movement built farms, schools and businesses; foraging is foreign to it.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Gender-based role divisions were central doctrine, and enterprises were built.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution by need is not part of the program, which emphasized work, discipline and enterprise.

production-for-use.rationale: The Nation ran profit-seeking bakeries and shops without a doctrine of production for need.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Muhammad's analysis of exploitation was racial rather than class-based, and the Nation ran profit-making enterprises.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Inferred; the movement is racial and religious rather than proletarian.

collective-farming.rationale: The Nation owned farmland, but whether it held collective farming as a principle is not stated.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not addressed; wars are attributed to the nature of whites in the Yakub account.

taxation-theft.rationale: The Nation demanded state funding for a black state, so a general rejection of taxation does not fit.

harm-principle.rationale: The Nation enforced strict personal moral discipline on members; inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Nation treats the black nation as a collective whose redress and separation are demanded as a group.

conscription.rationale: Muhammad told followers not to register for the draft and served prison time himself for draft evasion.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Separation, the right to leave integration behind, is the Nation's answer to its grievances, though the vote is not rejected outright.

state-as-business.rationale: No doctrine on running government like a business, though Muhammad was himself an enterprise builder.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not addressed, though the call for state support to the separate nation points to material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; Muhammad's schools disputed with school boards, but no thesis about media power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The Nation of Islam's Yakub teaching holds that whites were bred into a race with a violent and deceitful nature, a claim of inborn racial character; it is a theological origin story rather than a claim about genetic ability, so the fit is close but not exact.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation through families and trade bodies is not in the sources; the Nation's own structure was religious.

total-state.rationale: Inferred; the movement ran its own institutions but did not advocate a totalist state.

national-rebirth.rationale: The Nation preaches awakening the 'dead' black nation from enslaved decadence to its original divine status.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The Nation asked for a defined territory, not expansion abroad; Muhammad spoke of civilizing Africa.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The Nation's structure demanded personal loyalty to its messenger, but the statement concerns feudal political order, which is not addressed.

bound-labor.rationale: The Nation's founding grievance is slavery and bondage, so any bound labor is rejected.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The Nation taught that Christianity and white learning were instruments of white supremacy, and ran its own schools in response.

universal-morality.rationale: The Nation's morality is tied to race and revelation through its messenger, not universal reason.

single-common-good.rationale: No statement on a single reasoned common good; the Nation's concern was the racial interest of black people.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Muhammad ranked Orthodox Jews above most whites spiritually but taught that Jews were a Yakub-created race; inferred opposition, uncertain.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed beyond the Nation's own return to a black homeland.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed; the Nation said slavery stripped black people of their language, which hints at sympathy.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Democratic votes in company management are absent from the Nation's economic teaching.

school-vouchers.rationale: The Nation ran its own schools, which clashed with city school boards, so support for choosing private schooling is inferred.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

economic-freedom.rationale: Muhammad urged black enterprise, but no source links economic and political freedom as the statement does.

national-self-determination.rationale: The core demand is a separate state for black Americans governing themselves.

force-without-un.rationale: UN authorization of force is not addressed, and the Nation opposed black service in American wars.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The Nation rests on revelation from Fard Muhammad and Elijah Muhammad as messenger, and faith claims such as the Mother Plane.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The sources do not address who should receive welfare or any split between citizens and immigrants.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The Nation's self-help ethic stressed work and discipline; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Not addressed; internal black business ties were encouraged.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not addressed; the Nation sought to restore a lost heritage, which cuts against.

dominated-front.rationale: Malcolm X and Muhammad framed black Americans and non-European peoples as one 'Original Asiatic' family against white rule, though Pan-Africanism was rejected.

workers-nation.rationale: Class organisation along national lines is not in the sources; the Nation organised by race.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Men are providers, women household keepers, a core feature of Nation teaching.

ban-interest.rationale: The Nation has an Islamic framing and Muslim-style rules, but a ban on interest was not located in the sources; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Nation demanded racial separation, though it asked this as a negotiated separate state rather than white-run Jim Crow, which it also condemned.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Nation sees the state as a white instrument of racial domination, not of class.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is not discussed in the sources, so no basis for an answer.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The Nation rejected assimilation into white American culture.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not discussed; the Nation's goal was a separate state, not reform of voting rules.

national-mission.rationale: Muhammad said the Nation's job was to civilize Africa and awaken black people; inferred sense of mission.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The Nation endorsed male headship and does not treat it as an injustice.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Black and white elites are called out, including 'Uncle Tom' leaders and the federal government that will not protect black people.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Yakub's story involves eugenics, but state curbs on those with defects are not stated.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The Nation criticized police as heirs of slave patrols; inferred support for accountability.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Nation demanded a state-funded territory and spoke of an expansive moral order, not a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Members were to marry within the black community, and marrying whites was taboo; Malcolm X said only a man ashamed of himself marries out of his race.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Nation teaches blacks divine and whites devils by nature, so equal moral worth is denied.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The Nation had no socialist doctrine, so the question of socialism in one country does not arise.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed directly; the Nation saw the US as a white slave-holding state.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The Nation sought its own Islamic order apart from the existing American legal order; inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The Nation was a proselytizing faith that sought converts from Christianity.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; the Nation had food rules on pork but not cattle.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The Nation ran its own religious schools; the statement concerns state schools, on which it did not clearly stake out a view.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Socialist state theory is absent from Nation teaching.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The demand is for a separate state for people who do not consent to white rule; inferred from this.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade balance policy is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

population-transfer.rationale: The Nation proposed voluntary separation with state funding, and not forced expulsion of a minority; inferred.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Not addressed; the Nation's view is of racial struggle ordained by Allah, not progress by competition.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The Nation was itself persecuted as subversive and was prosecuted for sedition.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The framing of 6,000 years of rule over the black race as slavery fits a domination view, inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: The sources show no teaching on constitutional checks; the Nation sought a state but left its design unspecified.

vanguard-party.rationale: Not addressed; the Nation was led by a religious messenger.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The Nation recruited among the urban poor and prisoners, with programs of jobs and schools; inferred.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing is a British policy question absent from the Nation's concerns; no basis to infer.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strike law is not addressed in the sources, and the movement did not focus on labor disputes.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Poverty is blamed on slavery and white domination.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The program rests on the claim that integration cannot work and the races must live apart.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Selection of officials by lot is nowhere in the sources; no inference possible.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Nation ran its own newspaper but the sources say nothing on government control of media.

party-commands-army.rationale: A party commanding the army is not part of the Nation's teaching, which was a religious movement.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization rules are not discussed; the Nation's focus was black Americans, not immigrants.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay of elected representatives is not mentioned in the sources.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Members were bound by strict discipline in the Nation, but party legislators are not discussed.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The Nation sought its own sovereign state; inferred.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Executive command of the armed forces is not addressed in the sources.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Nation centred on a single messenger and ministers, and not bishops; not addressed as a political model.

clerical-rule.rationale: Authority rested on Elijah Muhammad as messenger of Allah, a religious leader at the head of the movement; inferred for a state.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Muhammad's followers refused the draft and he was jailed for it; inferred applicability to rival-power wars.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Strict moral discipline over members' conduct; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are not mentioned in the sources, so neutral.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of elected officials does not appear in the sources on the movement.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Military alliances are not discussed, though the Nation did oppose black participation in US wars.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; the Nation encouraged ownership but no ban.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Nation supported self-defense and had the Fruit of Islam, yet no stated demand for an armed citizenry.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Muhammad bought farmland and promoted agriculture for self-sufficiency; inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Divided-nation reunification has no analogue in Nation teaching.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: No documented view on university-educated people; the Nation did run its own schools.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The Nation ranks races, with blacks divine and whites devils, and rejects equality of peoples.

death-penalty.rationale: The sources record no Nation position on capital punishment.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The Nation's sexual morality is strict and abstinence-based; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The Nation has its own creation account with the Yakub story, but no stated position on public schools.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The Nation required chastity and modesty; inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship rules are not addressed in the sources, though the movement defines the nation by race.

minority-language-support.rationale: Muhammad's teaching said slavery took black people's language, but no policy on minority language support is recorded.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Muhammad's followers refused the draft on religious grounds; inferred support for exemptions.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The Nation enforced strict, uniform conduct among members.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Foreign debts are not discussed; the movement's demand was reparations from America.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Nation said independence needs black economic self-sufficiency, as Malcolm X urged black economic leadership in their own community.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-making procedure is absent from the sources.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The trade-off between freedom and development is not discussed in the sources.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The Nation demanded funding for black Americans from the former slave-owning nation; aid to the world's poor is inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear deterrence is not part of the Nation's teaching.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The sources do not say how a head of state should be chosen.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banking is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Land-for-peace deals are not addressed; the Nation's own demand was for territory.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The sources give no view on the grounds of private property rights.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Soviet Union's character is not a topic in the sources on the Nation.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk regulation never appears in the sources.

collective-defense.rationale: Not addressed; the Nation's Fruit of Islam defended its own members.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Annexation law is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The Nation judged policy by its doctrine of racial separation and prophecy, not by outcomes alone; inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The Nation's teaching holds that whites are devils to be destroyed by divine action and defends self-defense; absolute non-initiation is not its creed.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The movement suffered sedition prosecutions and police clashes; inferred opposition to suspending protections.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price fixing is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Nation of Islam built its own religious institutions and schools under its own authority and rejected the white-run state; inferred.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The Nation rejected the American political order and addressed no head-of-state question; neutral inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The Nation's own program demanded a separate black state and rejected the US government's claim over black Americans; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The Nation sought full separation, not autonomy inside the US, but would accept self-governing black institutions; split inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The Nation honoured Elijah Muhammad as messenger, but taught no divine descent for rulers and rejected the existing order; inferred.

flat-income-tax.rationale: No stated position on tax structure; the economic emphasis was on black-owned business.

character-from-environment.rationale: Its racial doctrine holds that races have innate natures, with whites bred as devils in the Yakub myth, though it also stressed moral reform; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Nation demanded justice and strict moral discipline and criticised rulers who broke their own law; inferred.

space-expansion.rationale: The Nation's teaching on space was mythic (the Mother Plane) and not about civilizational expansion; neutral inferred.

mixed-constitution.rationale: No stated position on constitutional form.

leader-cult.rationale: Elijah Muhammad was highly revered within the movement, but public leader glorification in national life was not a stated aim; neutral inferred.

equal-parenting.rationale: The Nation taught strict, differentiated gender roles with the father as head of the household; inferred from its family teaching.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The Nation of Islam framed the conflict as racial, not class-based, and was no socialist movement; inferred from its race-first program.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred from the demand for land for a separate black state and the Nation's own farmland purchases; it did not address breaking up estates as such.

refugee-return.rationale: The Nation sought separation, not return to former homes; no stated position, so inferred neutral.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Its territorial demand was for land inside the United States, not a claim abroad; no stated position on claims beyond borders.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred: the Nation disciplined its own members but as a minority did not seek state penalties for leaving a religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Members' women dressed modestly under Nation discipline, but it never asked the law to require covering; adherents' view is inferred.

common-currency.rationale: The Nation said nothing on currency; inferred neutral.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Elijah Muhammad taught a worldwide 'Asiatic' black nation and sought solidarity with Muslim and nonwhite peoples; inferred sympathy for cross-border unity.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the demand for a fully separate state rather than self-governing institutions inside the existing one.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Malcolm X stated that integration will not work and the Nation demanded a separate state rather than a fight for equal rights within white America.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Its history is a divine, race-based story (the Yakub myth) rather than an economic one; inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: No stated position on cartels or competition law; inferred neutral.

no-bailouts.rationale: No stated position on bailouts; the Nation stressed black self-reliance but said nothing on state rescues.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: As a persecuted minority it distrusted white majority rule but also demanded redress from the state; inferred mild lean against majority-only rule.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The Nation taught strict, separate gender roles for men and women; inferred opposition to parity quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The Nation urged black economic self-reliance within America, not a closed colonial trade bloc; inferred neutral on the literal claim.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: No stated position on trade agreements; inferred neutral.

moral-incentives.rationale: The Nation relied on moral discipline, duty and communal sacrifice rather than state incentives; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Malcolm X's 1963 statement limits force to self-defense, and the Nation refused military service; it did not seek to start a revolution by arms.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Its target was white privilege rather than inherited rank; no stated position on titles, so neutral.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Elijah Muhammad's schools and teaching centred black history and the Yakub account of race.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Nation taught that white rule was over and whites were devils, so rule over blacks by whites for their benefit is rejected.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Nation refused military service and sought separation from the United States, so national pride is not taught; inferred.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The program demanded separation and redress, not race-neutral rules; the sources do not discuss admissions or hiring preferences.

public-money-creation.rationale: No source addresses money creation; the stress on self-reliance gives no clear direction.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: No source addresses capitalism's crises; the Nation backed black-owned business inside the system.

former-empire-influence.rationale: No source addresses it; the movement was concerned with the United States, not former empires.

delink-world-market.rationale: The program sought a separate black state and economic self-reliance, so economic separation fits; inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Whites were seen as a ruling race, but the sources give no view on worker classes; inferred neutral.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The Nation opposed discrimination against blacks, though it also favoured separation; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The sources give no stated view; the Nation held that US law had not protected blacks.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of the white-ruled order and its legitimacy over black people.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred from the Nation of Islam's leadership under a single appointed Messenger rather than elected rule.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from a disciplined, hierarchical movement that does not give members a personal veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the belief that the white-ruled state was unjust and had no claim to obedience.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred from the movement's refusal to take part in electoral politics and its call for a separate state.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from the dietary and moral discipline the movement teaches, which counts harming animals as wrong.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from the same discipline, which permits eating permitted animals under rules.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from the movement's programme of mutual aid and duty within the black community.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Inferred from the movement's refusal to vote or join mainstream politics under Elijah Muhammad.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred from the claim that white-controlled media and culture keep black people subdued.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred from the teaching that white rule rests on deception and force, not on the consent of the governed.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred from the demand that the former slave-owning nation fund a black state for past unpaid labour.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from a programme that favours black leadership, not birthplace.

party-own-road.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on black self-determination under its own leadership.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Black economic self-reliance and separation from white institutions are core planks of the programme.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from a programme that seeks a new separate territory rather than recovering lost land.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from a doctrine that places black people in leadership above others, not the descendants of pre-colonial peoples.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of the white-led liberal order and its constitution.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred from a doctrine that does not frame politics around fascism and communism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred from a doctrine that places slavery at the centre of the white nation's crimes.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from its condemnation of white-run American history and its symbols.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred from strict gender roles that focus on the black man's duty and the woman's discipline.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from strict moral and gender discipline that treats violence by men and women unequally.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from its claim that black people have their own religion and way of ordering society.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from its refusal of military service and rejection of state institutions.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from its traditional gender roles, in which domestic work is the woman's duty.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the Nation of Islam's strict family and moral discipline; no stated doctrine on filial obligation.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred: authority in the Nation rested on the Messenger's appointment, and the movement said nothing for exam-based civil service.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from the stress on black economic self-reliance and distrust of white control of key resources.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the Nation's strict moral and gender discipline and emphasis on marital stability.

recallable-delegates.rationale: No stated position; the Nation was hierarchical internally but rejected white-run representative politics, so adherents' view is unclear.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Self-reliance points to private saving, while the demand for redress from the state points the other way; no stated position.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The Nation bought and held farmland privately and demanded a separate state, so it favoured ownership of land by blacks rather than tenure only by use.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: No stated position; the movement distrusted white-run government and legislatures and abstained from voting.

single-official-language.rationale: No stated position on a common state language; the Nation taught Arabic as a religious language but did not campaign on state language policy.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The demand for land for blacks is about a separate state, not a ban on foreign owners; no stated position.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Malcolm X's 1963 account treats the unequal condition of blacks as the result of white oppression, which implies judging policies by effect; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from the Nation's rules on thrift, diet, dress and against gambling and waste, which treat indulgence as harmful.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from Elijah Muhammad's refusal of military service and refusal to fight the government's wars.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from draft refusal and the rejection of the US state's wars; the Nation held that blacks should not fight for it.

corporate-influence.rationale: The movement saw the white-run economy as exploiting black people; inferred opposition to corporate power.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: No documented position; the movement sought black-run institutions free of outside control but distrusted the state.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Large families were encouraged, but incentives from the state are not documented.

residents-only-property.rationale: Its program demanded a separate black territory, so community-restricted land fits; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: Self-reliance through black-owned business was emphasised over state employment; adherents split.

democratic-peace.rationale: The movement rejected the white-led order and its claims of benevolence; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Members refused the draft and rejected obligation to a state of devils, though they kept their own discipline; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: The movement opposed white domination and colonial rule; inferred support for a bar on intervention.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The doctrine casts whites as devils against black people; this fits the statement only loosely, so inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Strict family and gender discipline were central to Elijah Muhammad's teaching.

local-production.rationale: Elijah Muhammad urged black economic self-reliance, including farms and shops; inferred support for local production.

informal-organisation.rationale: The Nation was a hierarchical organisation led by Elijah Muhammad with the Fruit of Islam, not informal.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The movement rejected US law but no source states a rule on international law.

religious-nation.rationale: The Nation of Islam defined its community through its religion alongside race, and religion is central to its program.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The doctrine rejects white dominance and ritual submission to other powers; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Regional revenue was not addressed; the program centred on a separate black state, so adherents' view is unclear.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Elijah Muhammad's program stressed black-owned private business and self-reliance rather than common ownership.

defeat-communism.rationale: The Nation of Islam opposed atheistic communism as incompatible with its religion; inferred.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: No source addresses service delivery; adherents are neither clearly for nor against.

religion-illusion.rationale: The Nation of Islam is a religious movement teaching Islamic doctrine and the Yakub story, so religion is not an illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Muhammad's program centred on black self-reliant business and called the white order evil; inferred as not progressive.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Nation enforced strict gender roles and moral discipline, and held that equality does not need economic transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: Strict family and gender roles imply domestic work stays in families; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purging is not addressed in the sources.

treaties-binding.rationale: Malcolm X's statement of the program demanded land and compensation for broken promises to black Americans; inferred support for binding commitments.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The program favoured a separate state and self-reliant economy rather than communal living; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: The doctrine rejects integration and favours separation, opposing steering majority settlement into minority regions.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Muhammad's program was black separatism and economic nationalism rather than either established system; inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred: the Nation of Islam demanded a separate black state and taught black people were the original people, but it grounded claims in grievance and divine destiny more than in ancestral land.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Inferred: Elijah Muhammad's teaching centred on white devilry and gave no program of Holocaust denial; this is a later-era controversy, so adherents are only leaning against.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from the strict moral and gender discipline the Nation of Islam imposed; it did not campaign on criminal law, so the legal step is uncertain.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Inferred: the movement was itself a persecuted minority seeking separation and self-rule, so it did not argue for suppressing opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred: the movement demanded separation rather than state enforcement of its religion on others, so state punishment of blasphemy is not part of the program.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred: the movement opposed white rule over non-white peoples and sought black self-determination.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: the Nation of Islam refused military service and stood outside mainstream Sunni doctrine, so adherents have no settled view on a jihad duty.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: the movement awaited divine judgment on white rule rather than preaching armed removal of rulers.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred: the Nation stressed disciplined, hierarchical, black-run institutions and said nothing on direct participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred: race was the organising axis and the movement kept strict, patriarchal gender roles, so it did not treat oppressions as overlapping.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the strict moral and gender discipline of the movement; the issue was not addressed.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from the movement's strict moral code and emphasis on preserving black life; not directly addressed.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred: the movement rejected both white-run parties and integration but did not frame its view as left-right synthesis.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: the movement attacked white exploitation of black labor but promoted black-owned business and work discipline, not a critique of work as such.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The Nation of Islam presented itself as Islam, so it rejects the claim that Islam is incompatible with the West, while also rejecting Western white society.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Inferred: Elijah Muhammad taught that Allah chose him as messenger and that divine law governed black life, though the program sought a state, not a theocracy.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred: the movement valued modest religious dress, and its women wore it publicly.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred: not addressed; no program on workplace law.

social-market-economy.rationale: Inferred: the movement favoured black economic self-reliance and ownership rather than either a welfare-market compromise or state economy.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Inferred: the movement refused military service in white wars but sought a state that would need its own defence.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred: its economic plan emphasised communal self-help and black ownership, not trickle-down.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred: the movement refused military service in wars of the white nation and urged separation from American power.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The Nation of Islam was led by Elijah Muhammad as a charismatic teacher with an appointed ministry, and says nothing on state succession; hereditary rule runs against its demand for its own separate state of believers, so only a weak inference.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Elijah Muhammad urged black-owned businesses and economic self-reliance; cost-based mutual banking is not documented, so this is an inference from that self-help program.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The Nation's program asked for a funded separate state and self-reliance, not a stance on IMF-style loan conditions, and adherents might see them as white power or as a reason for independence.

property-franchise.rationale: The Nation's program is not documented on franchise qualifications; Malcolm X's 1963 statement treats voting as of little use to blacks and nothing in it favours property tests, so a weak inference.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Nation of Islam teaching imposed strict gender discipline and patriarchal family roles, so it would not frame women's subordination as something to end, though it did not address nature.

reification.rationale: The Nation did not use Marxist categories; its economic teaching was about black self-reliance within a white-run economy, so no stated position on reification.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Malcolm X's account describes a white-controlled society where blacks lack real voice and power, so a hollow-rights claim would fit, though the press is not specifically discussed.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: No documented position on standing law and judges; the Nation distrusted white-run courts yet demanded equal justice under law, so adherents would not clearly agree or disagree.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Nation held that black people were the original, superior race and demanded a separate black state, so political rights confined to one racial group follows from its doctrine, though the program asked for separation rather than a racial franchise within one state.

online-participation.rationale: The Nation predates the internet and the movement's teaching is silent on online deliberation; no basis for a position.

open-government-data.rationale: Nothing in the Nation's documented program addresses open government records; it distrusted white-run government but did not campaign on transparency.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Malcolm X's 1963 statement rejects intermarriage between blacks and whites and Nation teaching stressed racial and religious separateness, but restriction by law is not documented, so only a weak inference.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The Nation urged black people to buy from black-owned shops, but its enemy was whites as a race, not a religious minority, and nothing documents shunning of religious-minority shops.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Elijah Muhammad ruled the Nation of Islam as God's Messenger and the program was disciplined, hierarchical and separatist; inferred that lot-chosen assemblies would be seen as foreign to it, though self-governing black institutions pull slightly the other way.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The Nation fixed its own doctrine (Yakub, the end of white rule) through Muhammad and rejected both mainstream Christianity and orthodox Islam, so adherents would reject outside updating of it; inferred, since it did not address reform of classical rulings.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Nation's economic program stressed black self-reliance and blamed white exploitation, but it did not make wealth concentration a threat to liberty as such; inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The Nation taught strict moral discipline and was hostile to homosexuality; inferred from that moral teaching, and it also refused military service.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Nation's teaching is religious, built on the worship of Allah and a theology of races, so promoting atheism in schools is opposed.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The Nation prized discipline and kept its own Fruit of Islam guard, and its program did not call for abolishing police; inferred.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The program demanded separation and a separate state, not shared government with whites; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Elijah Muhammad stressed black economic self-reliance and community institutions, though the program also demanded state funding; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: The Nation took no position on term limits; inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Malcolm X described the Nation as not voting and looking to separation rather than electoral politics, so delegable voting is of little interest; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The Nation's doctrine looks to the end of white rule, not to extinction risk; inferred.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The Nation's ministers were men and its teaching assigned women domestic and subordinate roles.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Nation taught strict gender discipline and the man as head of the family.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred: the Nation of Islam rejected participation in white-run American politics and sought a separate state, so voting by foreign residents is not a concern.

rent-control.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses rent controls; adherents are split between wanting state relief and relying on black self-help.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: black economic self-reliance meant building black-owned businesses, which rely on property rights, though abolition is not addressed.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The Fruit of Islam trained disciplined, uniformed male members and the Muslim Girls Training classes did the same for girls, which suits the doctrine's strict moral discipline.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: The doctrine does not address nuclear weapons; its separatist stance towards the American state suggests no stance on basing.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred: it rejected white governments' power over black people and sought separation, which tells against foreign troops, though it was not stated.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Elijah Muhammad taught that whites enslaved and killed black people and demanded redress; recognition of past mass killings of a people fits this, though not stated for genocide.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the stress on black self-reliance through work and business, and from the demand that the former slave-owning nation compensate black labour.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Elijah Muhammad taught that Muslims may defend themselves and should refuse military service; Malcolm X endorsed defence 'by any means necessary', so self-defence is not wrong.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The doctrine claims an unbroken black origin as the original people, though it is a religious lineage story and not a national continuity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine teaches fixed, divinely ordered roles for the sexes and says nothing on sex as socially constructed.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred: strict gender roles within a patriarchal family make the doctrine hostile to such feminist politics.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred: it honoured members who died for the nation of Islam, but its programme refused military service, so national martyrs is not a fit.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The Nation of Islam taught a cosmic struggle between the black original people and the white race of devils, with the end of whites' 6,000-year rule.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred: it sought a separate black state in America funded by the former slave-owning nation, rather than a homeland as a centre for a diaspora.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred: it stressed moral and spiritual regeneration of black people through discipline and religion as the basis for separation.

god-not-male.rationale: The Nation of Islam taught that Allah appeared in person as a black man, Wallace Fard Muhammad, and God is described as male.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine teaches male headship in a strict gender order and treats its teaching as scripture; judging by women's full humanity is not part of it.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Black economic self-reliance and black-run businesses were core; in a separate black state the economy would be in black hands.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The programme sought one separate state for black people, so unifying a people's regions is consistent with it, though not stated as an administrative proposal.

independent-unions.rationale: Nation of Islam teaching stressed black economic self-reliance but did not address union independence; inferred neutral.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Not addressed; the Nation of Islam pursued a separate black state and black capitalism, not a workers' power doctrine.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not addressed; the movement stressed black-owned businesses, and adherents are split on public provision.

second-chamber.rationale: Not addressed; the movement sought a separate state without stated institutional design.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred: the Nation of Islam promoted black-owned private enterprise and a separate state, not community ownership of production.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Not addressed; no stated position on confederal governance.

family-wage.rationale: The Nation of Islam taught strict gender roles with men as providers and protectors of the family, which fits a wage able to support a family.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; the Nation held health reforms of its own on diet but no view on regulators.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed; adherents distrusted the white-run government, but no stated position on payment privacy.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic for the 1934-1975 scope; no stated position.

person-over-state.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine centres on the black collective and the Nation's discipline, with mixed signals on individual versus group ends.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The Nation of Islam was a religious movement that taught that politics and the black nation's destiny serve divine ends, so it holds human beings to be spiritual as well as material.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Not addressed; no stated position on regional self-government.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic for the scope; no stated position.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed; the movement was urban but took no stated position on density.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Malcolm X's statement of the Nation's program and Elijah Muhammad's teaching held that black people have distinct interests requiring separation and organisation of their own.

racial-pride.rationale: The Nation of Islam taught that black people are the original and superior race and urged racial pride and self-respect against white supremacy.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The Nation refused military service in white America's wars, but its stated position on armed force in general is not a defensive-only rule; adherents are split.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The Nation of Islam defined the black nation by race and descent, not by language and history; inferred.

communal-electorates.rationale: Elijah Muhammad urged abstaining from white-run politics and seeking a separate state, so separate electorates are not on point.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The movement saw the white-run state as hostile but its concern was white rule, not partition of the country.

free-public-college.rationale: No stated position; self-reliance stressed black-run institutions.

pollution-taxes.rationale: No stated position; the movement said nothing on environmental policy.

future-generations.rationale: No stated position on this issue; inferred indifference.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Doctrine prescribed strict separate gender roles under male leadership; inferred that women's distinct weight in public life was not stressed.

arms-reduction.rationale: Adherents refused military service and denounced white-led wars; inferred mild support for cutting arms.

open-diplomacy.rationale: No stated position; the movement was outside the diplomatic system.

capital-controls.rationale: No stated position; economic self-reliance was emphasised instead.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The Nation of Islam urged black self-defense and would not accept a white state's monopoly on force.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Elijah Muhammad refused the draft and Nation members refused service in white America's wars.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The Nation stressed black-run self-help and says little on bargaining; inferred.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Self-reliance and black-owned enterprise were preferred to dependence on the white-run state; inferred.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The Nation addressed no fiscal rules; no inference is possible.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The Nation demanded redress from the former slave-owning nation; inferred sympathy with a fairer world order.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The Nation sought separation and awaited the fall of white rule rather than revolution to seize the state; inferred.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The Nation taught a set program of black economic self-reliance rather than open experimentation; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The Nation did not address ecosystems or natural capital.

sacred-nation.rationale: The Nation presented black people as a divinely chosen nation with lasting meaning; inferred from its theology.

student-debt-relief.rationale: The Nation did not address student loans.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The Nation held that black Americans were subordinated and exploited by white America, close to an internal colony; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Yakub doctrine holds that blacks are the original divine race and whites a bred race of devils, denying a shared human nature.

public-service-media.rationale: The Nation did not address public broadcasting; adherents distrust white-run media but the question is untouched.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Under Elijah Muhammad the Nation taught Islam as the true religion of the black man and condemned Christianity as the slave-master's religion, so it rejects equal-truth pluralism.

farm-price-support.rationale: Elijah Muhammad stressed black farming and land ownership, but the sources show no position on state price supports; adherents distrusted white-run government.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The Nation refused military service and stressed self-defense; no stated view on nuclear arms, so split.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Nation discouraged participation in white-run party politics and sought a separate state; inferred from Malcolm X's statement on voting.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the Nation's strict moral discipline and Islamic framing; it never taught or practised FGM.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The Nation taught strict gender roles and male protection of women, but black land ownership was a goal; no stated view on inheritance.

one-language-many-names.rationale: A linguistic classification question the doctrine never addressed.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: No stated position; adherents' self-reliance ethic and distrust of the state pull in opposite directions.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The Nation demanded separation and black-run institutions, not a role for customary chiefs in national law; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: No stated position on the environment; inferred neutral.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: The Nation taught that the white-run justice system was unjust to black people, so fixed harsh sentences would be opposed; inferred.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Under a separatist program the question of immigrants to a white-run nation is secondary; no stated view.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Nation of Islam teaching stresses black self-reliance and its own businesses and says nothing on union dues; inferred as no stated position.

voter-id.rationale: The Nation did not address ID rules; it urged separation from white-run politics, so no position is inferred.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The Nation held its own teaching to be the true Islam, so inferred to resist equal legal standing for rival interpretations.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The Nation distrusted electoral politics and abstained from it, but did not theorise democracy as procedure; split or indifferent.

premarital-sex.rationale: The Nation enforced strict sexual and gender discipline and confined sex to marriage.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a movement that was itself surveilled and distrustful of state power.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Economic program was black self-help and a funded separate state, not welfare design; no stated position.

women-suffrage.rationale: Women's vote was not an issue for the Nation, which stressed separate gender roles but abstained from politics generally.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred: the Nation made religion the centre of its teaching on women's roles and treated its discipline as protective, not oppressive.

race-social-construct.rationale: The Yakub myth teaches that races are real, bred groupings with inherent differences, the opposite of a constructed-category view.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from its traditional gender roles and distrust of the state; no stated position.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the Nation of Islam stressed black-owned business and land for a separate state, not first-come claims to unowned resources.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: No stated position; the movement distrusted white-run institutions, yet condemned white crimes against black people.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred: Nation of Islam teaching read the Bible and Yakub's story in its own symbolic terms and held that whites had corrupted the Bible.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from its strict gender discipline and separate male and female roles.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred: the movement stressed black ownership and self-help and rejected socialism and communism as white projects.

indirect-election.rationale: No stated position; the Nation had its own appointed hierarchy but made no case on electoral mechanics.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred: the Nation of Islam rejected American religion and separated from it, so it would not favour a national church.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from its demand for a separate black state; autonomy is a lesser form of the same separatism.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from its call for black self-determination over territory, though it asked for a funded state rather than a local vote.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: No stated position on colonial borders; adherents would be split between Pan-African and separatist views.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from Elijah Muhammad's strict diet, thrift and black self-reliance.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: No stated position; the movement spoke of black Americans, not of indigenous peoples elsewhere.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from its refusal of military service for its members, which fits opposing the draft for both sexes.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Elijah Muhammad's demand for a separate black territory implies a bond with and duty to defend a homeland; inferred from the separate-state program, not from a stated doctrine of ancestral land.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The Nation stressed strict discipline against drugs but also denounced white-run policing and lynching; inferred that adherents distrust unaccountable state killing.

close-ties-china.rationale: The Nation's separatist, anti-white-world outlook had no stated China policy; adherents are split or indifferent, so neutral.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The Nation spoke for black people as one people wherever they live; inferred support for protecting co-ethnics abroad.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The Nation promoted black private enterprise and landholding for self-reliance, which implies rejection of equal common ownership; inferred.

self-ownership.rationale: The Nation imposed strict bodily discipline (diet, no drugs or alcohol) under religious authority, so full personal rights over one's body are not its stance; inferred.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: No stated position on consumption taxes; self-help economics pulls toward lower taxes but adherents are not documented either way.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The Nation demanded redress for the poor black population while favouring self-reliance; inferred leaning toward aid aimed at the poorest.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The Nation was centred on a single leader and refused to take part in electoral politics; inferred that intermediaries are distrusted.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The Nation's critique of white-dominated economic power implies opposition to privileged white business interests; inferred.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The Nation is itself a religiously defined movement whose racial theology is its politics, so it does not separate politics from religion.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The Nation ran its own schools and businesses while upholding strict traditional moral and family discipline; inferred it would combine both.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The Nation taught strict gender roles and male headship in the family; inferred opposition to unilateral divorce by wives.

national-resource-control.rationale: The separate-state and black self-reliance program implies black or national control of resources rather than foreign (white) control; inferred.

distribution-by-process.rationale: The Nation of Islam held that whites had unjustly enriched themselves from slavery and demanded land and funding in redress, so process alone does not justify a distribution.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: No source addresses financial levies; the movement's economics centred on black-owned business.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Elijah Muhammad taught that the white race was devils and that oppression by whites continued, so racism is the main obstacle.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The movement held the white-run American order unjust and refused its military service, which implies that unjust law does not bind; inferred.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Anachronistic: the movement stressed black self-reliance and discipline of work and has no stated position on automation; inferred.

multipolar-world.rationale: The doctrine held that white rule had ended and favoured a separate black state, which suggests separate centres of power; inferred, not stated.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The movement's economics centred on self-help and black-owned business and no source states a labour theory of value; inferred neutral.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The movement rejected the American state and refused military service, so patriotism to the country is not shared, though service of black workers is; inferred.

material-over-identity.rationale: Its core claims on race, religion and separation put racial identity first; inferred it would not subordinate them to class politics.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The movement favoured black capitalism and religious discipline and had no communist link; inferred.

missingStatements.text: Some races are inherently superior to others.
missingStatements.rationale: The central doctrine is that black people are the original, divine race and whites an engineered race of devils.

missingStatements.text: Black Americans should receive land and public funding for a separate state of their own.
missingStatements.rationale: The Muslim Program demanded a separate state funded for 20 to 25 years by the former slave-owning nation.
missingStatements.declined: Specific historical demand of the Nation of Islam program, too narrow for the bank; reparations and separatism are covered by colonial-reparations and ethnic-nation.

missingStatements.text: Racial integration is neither possible nor desirable.
missingStatements.rationale: Malcolm X said integration will not work and called gains tokenism.

notes: Black supremacy is a label applied by outside watchdogs and used by a few historical figures such as Leonard Howell; it is not one organised ideology. After 1975 the Nation of Islam under W. Deen Mohammed dropped the doctrine and Louis Farrakhan's revived Nation retained it. Answers on most economic and institutional questions are inferences.
